b1-economiacolonial-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Potosí Grows
b1-economiacolonial-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are watching a documentary about Potosí, and he asks what happened to the city as silver production grew.
b1-economiacolonial-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the city as production grew.
cues: Say that silver production grew, with a medida que
Say that the city grew too
b1-economiacolonial-01.target: A medida que crecía la producción de plata, la ciudad crecía.
b1-economiacolonial-01.english: As silver production grew, the city grew.
b1-economiacolonial-01.canDo: I can use *a medida que* and *cuanto más …, más …* to say how two changes grew together.

b1-economiacolonial-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Forced Labour in the Mines
b1-economiacolonial-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are at a museum exhibition about colonial labour, and she asks what happened to the indigenous people in the mines.
b1-economiacolonial-02.prompt: Tell Meg what was done to the indigenous people in the mines.
cues: Say that the indigenous people were forced to work in the mines
b1-economiacolonial-02.target: Se obligaba a los indígenas a trabajar en las minas.
b1-economiacolonial-02.english: The indigenous people were forced to work in the mines.
b1-economiacolonial-02.canDo: I can use impersonal *se* to say what was done to people without naming who did it.

b1-economiacolonial-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Africans and the Plantations
b1-economiacolonial-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are reading a book about the sugar plantations, and he asks what happened to millions of Africans.
b1-economiacolonial-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what was done to millions of Africans.
cues: Say that they were taken to America by force
b1-economiacolonial-03.target: Millones de africanos fueron llevados por la fuerza a América.
b1-economiacolonial-03.english: Millions of Africans were taken to America by force.
b1-economiacolonial-03.canDo: I can use the passive with *ser* to say what was done to Africans in the plantation economy.

b1-economiacolonial-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Silver Reaches Asia
b1-economiacolonial-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are planning a trip to Seville, and she asks how American silver reached Asia.
b1-economiacolonial-04.prompt: Tell Meg how silver reached Asia.
cues: Say what happened to the silver, in the imperfect
Say by what means, with por medio de
b1-economiacolonial-04.target: La plata llegaba a Asia por medio del galeón de Manila.
b1-economiacolonial-04.english: Silver reached Asia by means of the Manila galleon.
b1-economiacolonial-04.canDo: I can use *a través de*, *por medio de* and *mediante* to say by what means things happened.

b1-economiacolonial-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Wealth and Problems
b1-economiacolonial-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a class on the colonial economy, and he asks whether Spain kept all the silver it received.
b1-economiacolonial-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the silver Spain received.
cues: Say that Spain received a lot of silver, with aunque
Say that an important part left the country
b1-economiacolonial-05.target: Aunque España recibía mucha plata, una parte importante salió del país.
b1-economiacolonial-05.english: Although Spain received a lot of silver, an important part left the country.
b1-economiacolonial-05.canDo: I can use *sin embargo*, *no obstante*, *aunque* and *a pesar de que* to contrast the benefits and the costs of silver.

b1-economiacolonial-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Silver Economy
b1-economiacolonial-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing for a class on the colonial economy, and she asks you to sum up what silver did to the Spanish crown.
b1-economiacolonial-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg what happened to the crown's wealth and debts.
cues: Use cuanto más … más … about silver and wealth
Add a contrast with sin embargo about the debts
b1-economiacolonial-consolidation.target: Cuanto más plata sacaban las minas, más riqueza llegaba a la corona; sin embargo, la corona tuvo muchas deudas.
b1-economiacolonial-consolidation.english: The more silver the mines produced, the more wealth reached the crown; however, the crown had many debts.
b1-economiacolonial-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the colonial economy with *cuanto más … más …*, impersonal *se*, the passive with *ser*, formal phrases of means and contrast connectors.
